children: Basis bids for soybeans shipped by barge to the US Gulf Coast were mixed on Thursday as the ongoing harvest in the southern US crop belt added to supplies available to Gulf exporters.
Chicago Board of Trade soybean and grain futures slumped on Thursday as traders waited to see whether a highly anticipated US-China summit would produce agricultural trade deals.

US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent told Fox News on Wednesday after talks with Chinese Vice Premier He Lifeng that they had agreed to extend until January 10 an agreement pausing a trade war that saw mutual tariffs top 100%.

However, traders hoped China would announce it would buy specific amounts of US crops or remove a 10% tariff on imports of US soybeans in conjunction with a meeting between Presidents Donald Trump and Xi Jinping in Washington.

At the Gulf, bids for CIF soybean barges loaded in September rose to 87 cents over Chicago Board of Trade November soybean (SX26) futures, and bids for October soy barges firmed to 96 cents over futures.
Bids dropped for barges loaded in December and February.
CIF Gulf corn basis bids were steady or weaker. Barges loaded in September were bid 45 cents over CBOT December futures and offered around 50 cents over futures.
